words.description: If something seldom happens, it doesn’t happen very often.
words.example: It seldom rains in southern Arizona.

words.description: To shave means to cut the hairs on your face with a sharp tool.
words.example: My father shaves his face every day because he doesn’t want a beard.

words.description: If you are terrified , you are extremely scared.
words.example: When I saw the ghost, I was absolutely terrified !

words.description: A wizard is a man who can do magic.
words.example: The wizard made gold fall from the sky.

words.description: Baggage is the set of bags that people take with them when they travel.
words.example: I’m taking several pieces of baggage with me on vacation.

words.description: A bulb is the glass part of an electric light.
words.example: I had to change the light bulb in my bedroom.

words.description: A bundle is a number of things that are tied together.
words.example: I was shocked when he showed me a bundle of money.

words.description: Cattle are cows and bulls, especially on a farm.
words.example: The rancher’s cattle were eating the grass in the field.

words.description: To flee means to run away from trouble or danger.
words.example: The crowd of men tried to flee from the danger.

words.description: To graze means to eat grass.
words.example: The cows grazed in the field.

words.description: Greed is a desire to have more than the things that you need.
words.example: She ate all the cookies out of her greed .

words.description: A herd is a large group of the same type of animals that live together.
words.example: The herd of cows moved slowly across the ranch.

words.description: To initiate something means to start it.
words.example: You have to turn the switch on to initiate the computer system.

words.description: A lane is a small road.
words.example: The lane passes directly in front of our house.

words.description: Nerve is bravery or the belief that you can do something.
words.example: He has the nerve to think that he can actually wrestle with a lion.

words.description: An optimist is somebody who sees the good parts of a situation.
words.example: Even though he has physical problems, my brother is an optimist .

words.description: A parade is a celebration when groups of people walk in the same direction.
words.example: There were many marching bands in the spring parade .

words.description: To pave the ground is to lay material on it to make it easier to walk or drive on.
words.example: The path was paved with yellow bricks.

words.description: A phantom is a ghost or spirit.
words.example: A scary phantom appeared from out of the darkness.

words.description: Something that is portable is able to be moved or carried easily.
words.example: Since computers are portable , people can use them anywhere.

words.description: A poster is a written announcement that is used to advertise something.
words.example: I saw a poster about a free concert in the park.

words.description: To scratch is to make small cuts with a claw or fingernail.
words.example: I used a stick to scratch my back.

words.description: A symphony is a long piece of music performed by many musicians.
words.example: Alex, a violin player, has always dreamt of playing a symphony .

words.description: A widow is a woman whose husband has died.
words.example: The widow had no children and was very lonely.

words.description: To circulate something is to spread it quickly.
words.example: The fan helped to circulate cool air through the room.

words.description: Consequent means happening because of a different situation.
words.example: Her consequent rash came after she touched the poison ivy.

words.description: To derive something from another source means to get it from that thing.
words.example: Red’s nickname was derived from the color of her hair.

words.description: To drown is to die from not being able to breathe underwater.
words.example: He would have drowned if the sailors would not have rescued him.

words.description: A dynasty is a series of rulers who are all from the same family.
words.example: The ancient Egyptians had a dynasty that lasted for many years.

words.description: A fraction is a small part of something.
words.example: Only a fraction of the cake was gone.

words.description: Frost is a white layer of ice that forms during very cold weather.
words.example: In the morning, the trees were all covered with frost .

words.description: An illusion is something that looks real, but doesn’t actually exist.
words.example: Some pictures create an illusion for the eyes.

words.description: To invade is to take over a place by force.
words.example: The enemy forces tried to invade our country through the air.

words.description: A lieutenant is a rank in the military or police, or a person with that rank.
words.example: The lieutenant was a good leader, and his soldiers respected him.

words.description: The word marine describes something related to the sea.
words.example: A healthy ocean is full of marine animals.

words.description: The merit of something or someone is their good qualities.
words.example: The actor received an award for his merits in the movie.

words.description: A navy is the part of a country’s military that fights at sea.
words.example: My country is known for our strong navy .

words.description: Polar relates to the cold places on Earth’s north and south ends.
words.example: Only a few people live in the Earth’s northern polar region.

words.description: A ray is a line of light that comes from a bright object.
words.example: The sun’s warm rays covered the beach.

words.description: To resign means to quit a job.
words.example: After I officially resigned from work, I said goodbye to my boss.

words.description: Suicide is the act of killing oneself.
words.example: Some people feel so sad that they think suicide is the only answer.

words.description: To tremble is to shake as a result of cold weather.
words.example: Harry was not used to the cold, so he trembled most of the day.

words.description: When something is underlying , it is a hidden cause of something else.
words.example: Her underlying fear of flying reduced her traveling options.

words.description: To travel via something means to travel through or using something.
words.example: We arrived in the city from the airport via the train.

words.description: To alter something means to make a small change to it.
words.example: I altered the color of my nails to match my hair.

words.description: If someone stands aside , they are on or to one side.
words.example: The man stood aside and opened the door for me.

words.description: Autumn is the season of the year between summer and winter.
words.example: I love when the leaves fall in autumn because I can play in them.

words.description: To blend is to mix two or more things together so that they become one thing.
words.example: My wife blended together all of the ingredients to make a delicious stew.

words.description: To collapse is to fall down suddenly.
words.example: The tree collapsed right in front of our house.

words.description: To crush something is to press it together so its shape is destroyed.
words.example: Selena’s new car was crushed when something fell on top of it.

words.description: To curve is to move in a line that bends and does not go straight.
words.example: The road curves to the left and to the right.

words.description: If something is disgusting , it is very unpleasant.
words.example: After running all day, Greg’s feet had a disgusting odor.

words.description: A drain is a pipe that carries away water from a building, such as in a kitchen.
words.example: The water in the sink goes down the drain as you wash your hands.

words.description: To embrace is to hug.
words.example: When they saw each other again, the happy couple embraced .

words.description: To envy someone is to wish that you had something that they have.
words.example: Sally envied the happy couple.

words.description: Fireworks are objects that create colored lights when they are lit.
words.example: The display of fireworks was so beautiful.

words.description: Flour is a powder made from plants that is used to make foods like bread.
words.example: I wanted to bake a pie, but I needed flour .

words.description: A fuse is a string that you light on fireworks to make them explode.
words.example: The boy litthe fuse on the rocket and waited for it to burst in the sky.

words.description: Ginger is a spice from the root of a plant. It tastes spicy and sweet.
words.example: Ginger is a common ingredient in many dishes from India.

words.description: If you are jealous , you think someone might take something from you.
words.example: Miriam was jealous because Sue was paying too much attention to Jim .

words.description: A paste is a thick and smooth substance.
words.example: My son needed some paste for a school project.

words.description: A receipt is a paper that proves that something was received or bought.
words.example: After looking at my receipt , I realized that I had spent too much money.

words.description: To wipe something is to slide a piece of cloth over it to clean it.
words.example: She wiped the dust from the windows.

words.description: A wire is a thin string made out of metal.
words.example: The wires were connected to towers that brought electricity to the city.

words.description: If you acknowledge something, you accept that it is true or that it exists.
words.example: The teacher acknowledged that the young student was hungry.

words.description: An ambassador is a government worker who works in another country.
words.example: The ambassador from Korea was in charge ofthe conference.

words.description: If someone is a blonde , they have light-colored hair.
words.example: My cousin is different from me. She is a blonde with blue eyes.

words.description: To conquer a country means to attack and take control of it.
words.example: The soldiers were trying to conquer the world.

words.description: To drag something means to pull it across the ground.
words.example: The dog was dragging his owner down the street.

words.description: To exaggerate is to say that something is bigger or better than it really is.
words.example: Jimmy wasn’t exaggerating about the seriousness of his injury.

words.description: Heritage is the collection of features of a society, such as language and religion.
words.example: Teepees are part ofthe heritage of the American Indians of the plains.

words.description: To insult someone is to say things that will hurt their feelings.
words.example: The girls insulted each other all afternoon.

words.description: Meanwhile means until something happens or while something is happening.
words.example: He wants to be a doctor in the future, but meanwhile , he works a regular job.

words.description: A necklace is a piece of jewelry that people wear around their necks.
words.example: Joyce received a lovely pearl necklace for her wedding anniversary.

words.description: A noble is a rich and powerful person.
words.example: The Queen invited a noble from a nearby country to dinner.

words.description: When something is precious , it is valuable and important.
words.example: In a desert, water can be more precious than money.

words.description: A prejudice is an unfair opinion about someone before you get to know them.
words.example: The company’s rules against gender prejudice must be enforced.

words.description: A rumor is a story that may not be true.
words.example: Carla was spreading rumors around the office.

words.description: A sin is something that is wrong for religious reasons.
words.example: Taking something that doesn’t belong to you is a sin .

words.description: A spectacle is an amazing sight.
words.example: Niagara Falls is quite a spectacle .

words.description: A stack is a pile of different things.
words.example: There was a stack of paperwork on his desk to complete.

words.description: If someone is suspicious of someone else, they do not trust that person.
words.example: Dad was suspicious ofthe caller on the line.

words.description: Tin is a cheap white metal.
words.example: Soup is a common food that is often sold in tin cans.

words.description: A vase is an attractive container where people keep flowers.
words.example: The vase was filled with such lovely flowers.

words.description: If something ache s, it hurts.
words.example: Mindy’s head ached because she bumped it against the wall.

words.description: If something is arctic , it is from far north near the North Pole.
words.example: It is cold when the arctic winds blow.

words.description: A canal is a path for water to travel through.
words.example: The city of Venice, Italy, has many canals .

words.description: A chemist is a scientist who works with chemicals.
words.example: My mother is a successful chemist who helps invent new products.

words.description: A chill is a feeling of cold.
words.example: The chill from the cold wind made Bill shiver.

words.description: Congress is a group of leaders in a government.
words.example: Congress makes laws for people to follow.

words.description: If something is dairy , it is made from milk.
words.example: Things like milk and cheese are dairy foods.

words.description: To descend is to go downward.
words.example: I descended the stairs to get out of the building.

words.description: A grocer is a person who sells food.
words.example: Our grocer , Mr. Smith, is a very kind man.

words.description: To hesitate is to wait for a short time before doing something.
words.example: He hesitated for a moment before he decided which choice to make.

words.description: An institution is an organization that works to help a city or group of people.
words.example: Banks are vital institutions that businesses and people use every day.

words.description: To jog is to run slowly.
words.example: He jogs every day so he can be healthier.

words.description: A merchant is a person who sells things.
words.example: The merchant was selling used cars.

words.description: To poke something is to push it with your finger.
words.example: I poked my finger on a thumb tack.

words.description: To postpone something is to make it happen later than planned.
words.example: They postponed the meeting until Elena arrived.

words.description: When a liquid splash es, it bursts and hits something.
words.example: Some green paint splashed upon the floor.

words.description: If people are stubborn , they don’t change their minds easily.
words.example: Both of my parents are stubborn . They never give in to each other.

words.description: A suburb is a small part of a large city.
words.example: I grew up in the suburbs only a few minutes outside of the city.

words.description: The tide is the level of the water in the sea.
words.example: The tide continued to crawl upon the beach little by little.

words.description: A tragedy is a very sad event.
words.example: It was a tragedy when his house was struck by lightning and burned.

words.description: A bomb is an object that explodes and destroys large areas.
words.example: The bomb will destroy anything that is near.

words.description: A certificate is a document that says that something is true or happened.
words.example: I was given a certificate after completing the computer course.

words.description: A circumstance is an event that makes a situation what it is.
words.example: There were many circumstances behind their success like hard work.

words.description: A coffin is a box used to bury dead people.
words.example: When a person passes away, they are usually buried inside of a coffin .

words.description: To cope with a difficult or stressful situation means to deal with it.
words.example: He copes with work stress by exercising three or four times a week.

words.description: Criticism is the act of saying that you don’t like or approve of something.
words.example: She had a lot of criticism about their new plan.

words.description: To devastate something means to completely destroy it.
words.example: The entire wall was devastated .

words.description: To frown is to make an unhappy look with your face.
words.example: Melissa frowned when she found out that the party had been cancelled.

words.description: To gaze at something means to look at it for a long time.
words.example: We used a telescope to gaze at the stars for over an hour.

words.description: To glance at something means to look at it quickly.
words.example: She glanced behind her to see if he was looking at her.

words.description: Grief is the feeling of deep sadness, usually when a person dies.
words.example: The grief caused by losing her parents was very difficult for her.

words.description: A groom is a man who is going to be married.
words.example: The groom looked happy as he walked with his new wife.

words.description: A license is an official document that gives one permission to do something.
words.example: In the United States you need a driver’s license to drive legally.

words.description: A microscope is a device that makes small objects look bigger.
words.example: Germs cannot be seen without a microscope .

words.description: When something is nuclear , it relates to the division or joining of atoms.
words.example: Nuclear power plants provide inexpensive energy to cities.

words.description: To portray something means to describe it or show it in a picture.
words.example: Her picture portrayed the house she grew up in when she was little.

words.description: To rotate something means to turn it around in a circle.
words.example: An airplane’s propellers rotate quickly to help it fly.

words.description: A souvenir is something you buy to remind you of a place or event.
words.example: I bought a Russian doll as a souvenir from my trip to Moscow.

words.description: A submarine is a boat that can go underwater for long periods of time.
words.example: The submarine dove under the sea so the enemy couldn’t see it.

words.description: To trace something means to follow over it with the eyes or a finger.
words.example: He traced over the graph with his finger.

words.description: An appliance is a piece of equipment used for jobs in the home.
words.example: Many homes have appliances like ovens, toasters and refrigerators.

words.description: A basin is large bowl for washing things. A sink is sometimes called a basin.
words.example: She filled the basin with water and washed her face.

words.description: A broom is a brush with a long handle used for cleaning floors.
words.example: My father usually uses a broom to sweep away dust in the basement.

words.description: A caterpillar is a small insect that looks like a worm and eats plants.
words.example: After eating a lot of leaves, caterpillars change into butterflies.

words.description: A cupboard is a piece of furniture that is used to store food or household items.
words.example: We put all of our dishes and food in the cupboards .

words.description: If something or someone is delicate , they are easy to break or harm.
words.example: You should hold the baby carefully because she’s very delicate .

words.description: To emerge from something means to come out of it.
words.example: The hand suddenly emerged from the grave.

words.description: A handicap is a condition that limits someone’s mental or physical abilities.
words.example: Joe has a slight handicap , so he uses a walker to get around.

words.description: A hook is a sharp curved piece of metal used for catching or holding things.
words.example: The fish went after the sharp hook .

words.description: To hop means to jump a short distance.
words.example: The kangaroo quickly hopped away from danger.

words.description: Laundry is clothes that have been or need to be washed.
words.example: He folded the clean laundry and put the dirty laundry in a basket.

words.description: To pursue someone or something is to chase or follow them.
words.example: The mother pursued her young child down the hill.

words.description: If someone is reluctant , they do not want to do something.
words.example: She was reluctant to eat the meager breakfast.

words.description: Sleeve s are the part of a shirt where your arms go.
words.example: Ryan bought a new shirt with long sleeves to keep his arms warm.

words.description: The spine is the bone that runs up and down the middle of the back.
words.example: Our spine helps us to stand up nice and straight.

words.description: A stain is a dirty mark that is difficult to clean.
words.example: He had a red stain on the collar of his shirt.

words.description: A strip is a long, narrow piece of material or land.
words.example: He had long strips of film that held images of his trip abroad.

words.description: To swear means to promise to do something.
words.example: I will put my hand on the Bible and swear to do my best for the country.

words.description: To swing something means to move it back and forth or from side to side.
words.example: He can swing a golf club very powerfully.

words.description: To utilize something means to use it for a specific purpose.
words.example: They utilized a pair of scissors to cut the ribbon.
